discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter / quantum optics (superconducting quantum circuits)
motivation: Blais, Schoelkopf and colleagues proposed in 2004 that a superconducting qubit coupled to a coplanar microwave resonator could reproduce cavity QED on a chip. Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated this the same year, observing vacuum Rabi splitting with a single artificial atom and a single photon in the strong-coupling regime. Circuit QED transformed quantum optics: it gave dispersive qubit readout, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, microwave Fock and cat states, on-chip quantum communication, and later the ultrastrong-coupling regime. It is now the architecture used by essentially every superconducting quantum processor worldwide. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in Josephson circuits. Circuit QED is the separate, later discovery that turned these circuits into a controllable light–matter laboratory and a scalable quantum technology. The work is clean, has been reproduced many times and has founded a whole field.
